descripcion_experiencia: This experience introduces visitors to the community of Eugenio Echeverría Castellot II and the El Hormiguero archaeological site through two options. The first begins at sunrise with a two-kilometre walk or bicycle ride from the lagoon to the archaeological site and ends with a regional breakfast at the ecotourism centre. The second begins in the afternoon at El Hormiguero, follows the trail to the lagoon and ends in the community, where visitors may camp and enjoy a dinner prepared by local women.

se_promueve: Environmental education related to ecotourism.

Además, desafiarás tus límites en su Centro Ecoturístico practicando senderismo, trail running, alpinismo o ciclismo de montaña rodeado por la majestuosidad de sus paisajes naturales.

nombre_experiencia: Visit to the Cave of the Hanging Snakes
anfitrion: Centro Ecoturístico Beej Ka’ax Ha, Kantemó
servicios_incluidos: Guided cave tour, observation of bats and hanging snakes, and interpretation of the ecosystem.
descripcion_experiencia: The night-time visit begins with a bicycle ride through the forest to the Cave of the Hanging Snakes. With local guides, visitors observe how non-venomous blotched rat snakes wait for different bat species as they leave the cave. The tour also reveals aquatic fauna adapted to darkness and fossils visible on the cavern walls.

nombre_experiencia: Swimming in the Chunyaxché Lagoon Channels
anfitrion: Muyil Conjunto de Aluxes, S.P.R. de R.I
servicios_incluidos: Boat tour through the Chunyaxché channels, wildlife observation and tasting of traditional food.
descripcion_experiencia: In the Sian Ka’an Biosphere Reserve, this experience crosses Chunyaxché Lagoon and an ancient channel built by the Maya. Accompanied by a local guide, visitors pass through different ecosystems, observe biodiversity and float in a clear freshwater channel. The route then continues towards the Boca Paila estuary, where wildlife such as manatees may be seen, and ends with a Maya meal at the Muyil community centre.

servicios_incluidos: 1. Servicios de Guías Guía especializado en Turismo Biocultural: Acompañamiento por un intérprete del patrimonio o guías locales capacitados que narra la historia arqueológica, agraria y mística. Anfitriones Locales: Pagos a los tlachiqueros y dueños de tinacales por el tiempo dedicado a la enseñanza y demostración de sus saberes. 2. Entradas y Accesos a Sitios Patrimoniales Zona Arqueológica de Zultépec-Tecoaque: Gestión de acceso al sitio y recorrido por su Museo de Sitio. Acceso a Haciendas (Mazapa o San Cayetano): Cuota de entrada y permiso de fotografía en las instalaciones de las ex- haciendas pulqueras. Contribución a Áreas Ejidales: Pagos por el derecho de paso en los senderos y magueyeras que pertenecen a los ejidatarios de la comunidad de Tepuente. (temporada de luciérmagas) 3. Talleres y Materiales (Recuerdos Físicos) Taller de de educación ambiental adopta un maguey con tu nombre. Kit de Bienvenida (Opcional según paquete): incluye un jarrito de barro artesanal para las degustaciones. 4. Experiencia Gastronómica Completa Desayuno Campirano o Ritual de Bienvenida: Café de olla, pan de pulque o antojitos locales. Comida Tradicional en Tepuente: Menú completo servido por las cocineras tradicionales, que incluye: Platillo fuerte a base de maguey (mixiote, carne al pulque o ximbó). Complementos de la milpa (sopa de milpa, frijoles de la olla, salsas de molcajete). Agua de fruta natural o bebida local. Degustación Ilimitada (Cata): Aguamiel fresco de la mañana, pulque natural "de punta" y curados de temporada en los tinacales de Tepuente. 5. Conservación y Seguro Cuota de Conservación: Un porcentaje del pago se destina a la reforestación de magueyes (el programa "Adopta un Maguey") y mantenimiento de suelos. Seguro de Viajero: Cobertura de gastos médicos básicos durante el recorrido.

descripcion_corta: Vive una inmersión en comunidades nahuas de Atlahuilco. Aprende alfarería y telar, explora cuevas sagradas y la medicina tradicional. Convive con familias locales y degusta su gastronomía apoyando la preservación del patrimonio biocultural.

descripcion_experiencia: Descubre Sontecomapan en la Reserva de la Biosfera Los Tuxtlas. Vive una aventura auténtica navegando entre manglares, recorriendo selvas tropicales y disfrutando de playas vírgenes. Conoce la vida de los pescadores locales, su compromiso con la conservación y deléitate con su exquisita gastronomía regional.
descripcion: Descubre Sontecomapan en Los Tuxtlas. Navega entre manglares, recorre selvas tropicales y disfruta playas vírgenes. Conoce a los pescadores locales, apoya su compromiso con la conservación y deléitate con su exquisita gastronomía regional.

descripcion_experiencia: Recorre cristalinas pozas, cascadas y cuevas mientras te sumerges en talleres artesanales, apicultura y el cultivo de malanga. Disfruta una gastronomía local única, desde atoles hasta platillos típicos, en una experiencia que transforma la conservación en un viaje inolvidable.
descripcion: Recorre pozas cristalinas, cascadas y cuevas. Sumérgete en talleres artesanales, apicultura y cultivo de malanga. Disfruta de atoles y platillos típicos, en una experiencia que transforma la conservación en un viaje inolvidable.
descripcion_corta: Recorre pozas cristalinas, cascadas y cuevas. Sumérgete en talleres artesanales, apicultura y cultivo de malanga. Disfruta de atoles y platillos típicos, en una experiencia que transforma la conservación en un viaje inolvidable.

servicios_incluidos: Incluye la arresania elaborada por el cliente, préstamo del molde, herramientas
descripcion_experiencia: Descubre Ojoxapan, una joya a orillas del Lago de Catemaco. Acompaña a las artesanas "Flor de Lirio" en un recorrido por el ecosistema lagunar, aprende a transformar el lirio acuático en artesanías únicas y explora cascadas escondidas. Vive una inmersión auténtica en la cultura, gastronomía y saberes de esta comunidad.
descripcion: Descubre Ojoxapan en el Lago de Catemaco. Acompaña a las artesanas "Flor de Lirio", explora el ecosistema lagunar, cascadas escondidas y transforma el lirio en artesanías. Sumérgete en la cultura, gastronomía y saberes locales.
descripcion_corta: Descubre Ojoxapan en el Lago de Catemaco. Acompaña a las artesanas "Flor de Lirio", explora el ecosistema lagunar, cascadas escondidas y transforma el lirio en artesanías. Sumérgete en la cultura, gastronomía y saberes locales.

descripcion_experiencia: Descubre Ceytaks, un refugio popoluca en Veracruz donde la historia olmeca cobra vida. Explora cascadas espectaculares, tirolesas y puentes colgantes rodeado de orquídeas y monos aulladores. Deleita tu paladar con auténtico molito de pollo de rancho y platillos tradicionales de temporada.
descripcion: Descubre Ceytaks, refugio popoluca en Veracruz donde la historia olmeca revive. Explora cascadas, tirolesas y puentes colgantes entre orquídeas y monos aulladores. Deléitate con molito de pollo de rancho y ricos platillos de temporada.
descripcion_corta: Descubre Ceytaks, refugio popoluca en Veracruz donde la historia olmeca revive. Explora cascadas, tirolesas y puentes colgantes entre orquídeas y monos aulladores. Deléitate con molito de pollo de rancho y ricos platillos de temporada.

descripcion_experiencia: Reconecta con tu esencia en el Centro Ecoturístico Jomxuk, un refugio popoluca en la Sierra de Santa Marta. Vive el ritual del Dios del Maíz, recorre el "Sendero del Silencio" y habita la naturaleza en total plenitud. Disfruta de una estancia que honra la sabiduría ancestral y la medicina tradicional.
descripcion: Reconecta en el Ecoturístico Jomxuk, refugio popoluca en la Sierra de Santa Marta. Vive el ritual del Dios del Maíz, explora el "Sendero del Silencio" y disfruta una estancia que honra la naturaleza, medicina y sabiduría ancestral.

descripcion_experiencia: Descubre Kantajsekan, el "Lugar de Sombras" en la Sierra de los Tuxtlas. Esta comunidad nahua te invita a una aventura sustentable entre senderos, cascadas y ríos. Disfruta tirolesas, kayak y ciclismo mientras te sumerges en su identidad, gastronomía y tradiciones ancestrales.
descripcion: Descubre Kantajsekan en Los Tuxtlas. Esta comunidad nahua te invita a una aventura sustentable entre senderos, cascadas y ríos. Disfruta tirolesa, kayak y ciclismo, sumergiéndote en su identidad, gastronomía y tradiciones.
descripcion_corta: Descubre Kantajsekan en Los Tuxtlas. Esta comunidad nahua te invita a una aventura sustentable entre senderos, cascadas y ríos. Disfruta tirolesa, kayak y ciclismo, sumergiéndote en su identidad, gastronomía y tradiciones.

descripcion: Disfruta en Vida Milenaria el campamento tortuguero y glamping frente al mar de Tecolutla; con actividades como la liberación de crías de tortugas, el avistamiento de la anidación y el manejo responsable de la fauna marítima.
descripcion_corta: Disfruta en Vida Milenaria el campamento tortuguero y glamping frente al mar de Tecolutla; con actividades como la liberación de crías de tortugas, el avistamiento de la anidación y el manejo responsable de la fauna marítima.

anfitrion: Víctor Chim Vergara y Lourdes Canché
servicios_incluidos: Interpretive tour of Aktun Usil cave, observation of Maya paintings and remains, welcoming ritual and optional traditional meal.
capacidad_grupo: Small groups to support visitor control and cave conservation.
descripcion_experiencia: Aktun Usil is a high-ceilinged cave whose name refers to the place where painted lines can be seen. Inside are paintings, altars, fragments of vessels, ceramics and other remains associated with Maya culture. Certified local guides lead the visit, interpret the underground landscape and share the site’s stories and legends.
patrimonio_material: Pre-Hispanic paintings on the cave walls, pre-Hispanic carvings of Maya figures and symbols in the cave’s stones, and a striking view of the Puuc region from the highest part of the site.
patrimonio_inmaterial: Maya welcoming ritual for visitors, accompanied by phrases in the Maya language and copal incense.
patrimonio_natural: Reforestation of the trail to the cave with local trees and conservation of the trees and wildlife surrounding the cave entrance.
personas_involucradas: Certified tour guides under NOM-08, maintenance staff, mototaxi drivers transporting visitors to the cave and traditional cooks.
productos_locales: Traditional Yucatecan food available by advance booking.
se_fomenta: The care and conservation of the cave.
se_promueve: Learning about Maya culture.
fuente: Maya World Mexico Tourism Experiences Catalogue, UNESCO / Maya World Mexico Alliance, 2025

servicios_incluidos: Yucatecan Maya cooking workshop, collection of ingredients, preparation of dishes and dessert, restaurant and optional rural accommodation.
descripcion_experiencia: Xbatun Village offers an ancestral cooking workshop in a setting of traditional Maya architecture. Guided by local cooks, participants collect ingredients from the household garden and prepare starters such as sikil pak, encamisado and dzotobichay, as well as pollo pibil and a cacao dessert. The experience can take place during the day or as an evening meal and includes restaurant and rural accommodation options.
patrimonio_material: The palapas used for cooking, accommodation huts, the Maya oven or pi’ib, traditional clothing and the traditional Maya cultivation system known as ca’anché.
patrimonio_inmaterial: Traditional culinary knowledge passed down through generations and the Maya language.
patrimonio_natural: The organic garden that supplies some of the ingredients used in the kitchen.
personas_involucradas: The family, whose members share responsibilities for cooking, leading the workshop, coordinating activities, handling bookings and maintaining the site.
productos_locales: Ancestral and Yucatecan cuisine, including sikil pak, encamisado, dzotobichay and pollo pibil.
se_fomenta: Ancestral Maya culinary techniques.
se_promueve: Visitors’ active participation in cooking techniques.
fuente: Maya World Mexico Tourism Experiences Catalogue, UNESCO / Maya World Mexico Alliance, 2025

servicios_incluidos: Chocolate-making workshop, roasting and hand-grinding cacao, tasting and preparation of chocolate tablets to take home.
capacidad_grupo: Small groups, respecting the capacity of the Maya house.
descripcion_experiencia: Caricoa invites visitors to learn the artisanal process used to make table chocolate and the family’s traditional recipe. Participants roast cacao on a comal, grind the ingredients by hand, prepare the paste and mould their own tablets. At the end, they can taste the product and take home the pieces made during the workshop.
patrimonio_material: The Maya house where the experience is offered.
patrimonio_inmaterial: The knowledge and preparation techniques learned and preserved by the family.
patrimonio_natural: Natural ingredients, especially cacao, the main ingredient.
personas_involucradas: Dalia and her family.
productos_locales: Artisanal chocolate tablets and cacao-based products.
se_fomenta: Visits to immersive experiences.
se_promueve: Appreciation of this gastronomic activity.
fuente: Maya World Mexico Tourism Experiences Catalogue, UNESCO / Maya World Mexico Alliance, 2025

servicios_incluidos: Guided cave tour, visit to and swimming in the cenote, trails, local cuisine and optional accommodation.
descripcion_experiencia: Zazil Tunich offers an underground route of approximately 200 metres descending into a cave with stalactites and stalagmites. The path passes formations known as the Maya Kiss and the alux cave before reaching a shallow-water cenote. The visit is guided and may be complemented with trails, local gastronomy and accommodation.
patrimonio_material: Visitor facilities and cabins for accommodation.
patrimonio_inmaterial: A cultural performance inside the cave, including a Maya ceremony conducted in the Maya language.
patrimonio_natural: Cave-cenote and Yucatecan forest.
personas_involucradas: Local employees in different roles.
productos_locales: The cenote tourism experience, regional food, natural local beverages and a cacao-based drink.
se_fomenta: A guided tour that presents the history of the cave.
se_promueve: The care of the cave and cenote.
fuente: Maya World Mexico Tourism Experiences Catalogue, UNESCO / Maya World Mexico Alliance, 2025

servicios_incluidos: Demonstration class on Yucatecan cooking, preparation over a hearth and in a pib, and tasting of a four-course meal.
descripcion_experiencia: At Ya’axché, participants explore the spirituality and knowledge of Maya cuisine from western Yucatán. The class uses local ingredients and ancestral techniques, including the three-stone hearth and the underground oven or pib. The process takes place outdoors and ends with a tasting of the four-course meal prepared during the activity.
patrimonio_material: The vegetable garden, milpa, restaurant, kitchen and spaces used for the workshop.
patrimonio_inmaterial: The techniques and years of research the chef has devoted to the cuisine.
patrimonio_natural: The land where crops are grown and the pib is prepared.
personas_involucradas: Chefs, cooks, students and local residents.
se_fomenta: Local gastronomy.
se_promueve: The use of ancestral techniques.

servicios_incluidos: Tour of the jipijapa process, visit to the plantation and weaving cave, hands-on demonstration and sale of handicrafts.
descripcion_experiencia: The visit to Cuch Holoch presents the complete process of making jipijapa hats. The tour includes the plant from which the fibres are obtained, the cave where the pieces are woven in humid conditions and the space where heat is used to set their final shape. Participants can practise part of the weaving process and, at the end, view and purchase hats and other crafts in natural or dyed colours.
patrimonio_material: The family home where the materials used to make hats are stored.
patrimonio_inmaterial: The jipijapa weaving technique.
patrimonio_natural: The cave where the hats are woven and the land where jipijapa is cultivated.
personas_involucradas: A group of community artisans.
productos_locales: Hats for women and men, fans, tortilla baskets, jewellery boxes and other items.
se_fomenta: Visits to immersive craft experiences.
se_promueve: The purchase of jipijapa hats.
fuente: Maya World Mexico Tourism Experiences Catalogue, UNESCO / Maya World Mexico Alliance, 2025

descripcion_corta: Tour of the jipijapa process, visit to the plantation and weaving cave, hands-on demonstration and sale of handicrafts.

servicios_incluidos: Adventure tour of Grutas Chocantes with a guide, harness and safety equipment, drinking water, changing rooms and use of facilities.
capacidad_grupo: Small groups to maintain control and safety.
descripcion_experiencia: Grutas Chocantes offers an exploration of an underground karst landscape with stalactites, stalagmites and formations known locally as crystals. The adventure route is completed with a guide and safety equipment. On the surface, visitors may also enjoy zip-lining and rappelling at Gruta del Toro while learning about the history of expeditions carried out at the site.
patrimonio_material: On-site facilities, including the reception palapa, zip-line towers and specialised equipment.
patrimonio_inmaterial: Guide training, the history of the caves and their importance in Maya culture.
patrimonio_natural: The cave and its stalactite and stalagmite formations.
personas_involucradas: Maya Indigenous members of the cooperative.
productos_locales: Traditional Yucatecan food and local crafts made from semi-precious stones such as jade.
se_fomenta: The use of protective equipment when entering the cave.
se_promueve: Guided visits to improve safety and protection.
fuente: Maya World Mexico Tourism Experiences Catalogue, UNESCO / Maya World Mexico Alliance, 2025

servicios_incluidos: Local guide, stingless-bee ceremony, visit to the apiary and honey tasting.
capacidad_grupo: Small groups due to site capacity.
descripcion_experiencia: At the Lool-Há Stingless-Bee Apiary, Maya women share ceremonies connected with caring for bees and seasonal flowering. The experience includes a ritual in the Maya language, a visit to the space where stingless bees are raised and an explanation of their cultural and medicinal importance. It ends with a honey tasting and an introduction to products derived from this ancestral practice.
patrimonio_material: The palapas and land where the activity takes place.
patrimonio_inmaterial: The knowledge of the women who conduct the Maya ceremony.
patrimonio_natural: Stingless bees, honey and related products.
personas_involucradas: The ten women members of the organisation.
se_fomenta: Respect for the Maya ceremony.
se_promueve: The care and protection of stingless bees.
fuente: Maya World Mexico Tourism Experiences Catalogue, UNESCO / Maya World Mexico Alliance, 2025

descripcion_corta: Local guide, stingless-bee ceremony, visit to the apiary and honey tasting.

servicios_incluidos: Food-preparation workshop, traditional beverage, tour of Santa Elena and tasting of Yucatecan cuisine.
descripcion_experiencia: At Xa’ Anil Naj Maya Village, traditional cooks welcome visitors into a house built in the local architectural style. With their guidance, participants prepare pollo pibil in an underground oven, handmade tortillas and sikil pak using ingredients from the household garden. The activity also explains the meaning of practices associated with maize and, depending on the season, may include the ceremonial drink saká.
patrimonio_material: The Maya hut, hearth and Maya oven or pib.
patrimonio_inmaterial: Yucatecan recipes and the techniques used to prepare them.
patrimonio_natural: Organic ingredients from the region.
personas_involucradas: Family members who participate in the project.
se_fomenta: The preparation of traditional food.
se_promueve: The use of locally produced organic ingredients.

servicios_incluidos: Guided tour of Uayma and pottery workshop, from selecting the clay to shaping and firing the pieces.
capacidad_grupo: Small groups; the experience can be adapted to visitors’ needs.
descripcion_experiencia: This experience introduces visitors to pottery through a family that has worked with clay for several generations. A guided visit to central Uayma presents its seventeenth-century church, followed by a workshop where artisans explain each step of pottery production, from selecting and collecting clay to firing the finished pieces. The visit must be arranged in advance with the host to confirm availability, schedules, prices and participation conditions.
patrimonio_material: Uayma’s seventeenth-century colonial church and the pottery workshop.
patrimonio_inmaterial: Traditional clay pottery techniques and the pottery tradition of the Espadas family and Juanita Dzul Cob.
personas_involucradas: The Espadas family and local artisans.
se_fomenta: The preservation and transmission of traditional pottery.
se_promueve: Hands-on learning and recognition of local artisanal work.
fuente: Maya World Mexico Tourism Experiences Catalogue, UNESCO / Maya World Mexico Alliance, 2025

servicios_incluidos: Tour of Kanxoc, hands-on hand- or machine-embroidery workshop, introduction to textile products and local food.
capacidad_grupo: Small groups, according to the capacity of the home workshop.
descripcion_experiencia: Embroidery is one of Yucatán’s most distinctive heritage expressions. This experience allows visitors to learn selected hand- and machine-embroidery techniques. A local artisan provides practical instruction in traditional embroidery and the creation of textile and jewellery products.
patrimonio_inmaterial: Hand and machine Maya embroidery techniques, textile traditions and artisanal jewellery-making.
personas_involucradas: Ten cooperative members participate on a regular basis.
productos_locales: Traditional embroidery, textile products and artisanal jewellery.
se_fomenta: The continuity of traditional embroidery techniques.
se_promueve: The participation of women artisans and the purchase of community products.
fuente: Maya World Mexico Tourism Experiences Catalogue, UNESCO / Maya World Mexico Alliance, 2025

descripcion_corta: Tour of Kanxoc, hands-on hand- or machine-embroidery workshop, introduction to textile products and local food.

servicios_incluidos: Visit to the stingless-bee apiary and community garden, talk on native bees and tasting of different honeys.
descripcion_experiencia: Visitors can taste honeys produced by different native bee species and learn about their environmental and cultural importance in the Maya world through an engaging conversation with local women producers. The experience includes a visit to the stingless-bee apiary and community garden, a talk on native bees and stingless beekeeping, and tastings of honeys from different bee species and flowering seasons. The visit must be arranged in advance with the host to confirm availability, schedules, prices and participation conditions.
patrimonio_inmaterial: Maya stingless beekeeping and knowledge of native bees and their role in the Maya worldview.
patrimonio_natural: Native bee colonies and a community garden of nectar-producing plants.
personas_involucradas: A group of women stingless beekeepers.
productos_locales: Honeys from different native bee species and flowering seasons.
se_fomenta: The conservation of native bees and Maya stingless beekeeping.
se_promueve: Environmental education and the responsible consumption of local honey.

servicios_incluidos: Community tour with options including a bakery, embroidery, local gastronomy, a guayabera factory and everyday life in Tekit.
descripcion_experiencia: This community tour highlights the knowledge and practices associated with Tekit’s agricultural and intangible cultural heritage. Visitors learn about daily life in a town that continues to practise sustainable traditions while changing rapidly in response to textile industrialisation. They may choose to visit a local bakery, tour an embroidery workshop, take a gastronomic tour with a local cook or visit a guayabera factory.
patrimonio_material: Guayabera factory and traditional bakery.
patrimonio_inmaterial: Traditional gastronomy, Maya embroidery and guayabera production.
personas_involucradas: Bakers, embroiderers, cooks and local producers.
se_fomenta: Appreciation of Tekit’s agricultural, textile and gastronomic practices.
se_promueve: The participation of community businesses and families.
fuente: Maya World Mexico Tourism Experiences Catalogue, UNESCO / Maya World Mexico Alliance, 2025

servicios_incluidos: Visit to a Maya household garden, explanation of its components, breakfast or lunch made with seasonal products and access to a local shop.
descripcion_experiencia: Visitors have the opportunity to explore a Maya household garden and learn about its different components. The experience shows how knowledge from the past can be harmonised with present-day practices while respecting the environment and remaining part of everyday life. It includes a guided visit to the garden and an explanation of how its elements work together.

patrimonio_inmaterial: Agroecological knowledge associated with the Maya household garden and seasonal gastronomy.
patrimonio_natural: Seasonal plants in the garden and the local milpa.
personas_involucradas: Host family and local producers.
productos_locales: Handmade tortillas, sauces, regional beverages, artisanal ice cream, honey and herbal products.
se_fomenta: The revival of the Maya household garden and its agroecological knowledge.
se_promueve: The consumption of local products and low-impact environmental practices.

servicios_incluidos: Demonstration and workshop on traditional Yucatecan cooking, preparation over a hearth or in a pib, and tasting.
descripcion_experiencia: This experience takes place in a traditional Yucatecan restaurant where visitors learn and practise cooking techniques using a three-stone hearth, firewood and an underground oven or pib. Guided by Doña Marta, participants prepare dishes such as cochinita pibil, poc chuc, mucbipollo, huevos encamisados and tortillas made with nixtamalised maize. The workshop combines culinary learning, stories about daily life in Maní and a tasting of the food prepared.

descripcion_experiencia: This experience explores the natural surroundings of Sisal, characterised by mangroves, freshwater springs and dunes. The tours showcase abundant wildlife, especially birds, and three mangrove species: black, red and white. Because of their capacity to capture carbon, these ecosystems provide important environmental services. The visit must be arranged in advance with the host to confirm availability, schedules, prices and participation conditions.
